index-v2.html.text: Frequently asked questions What is Bridgify? What is experiences infrastructure? How do travel brands launch experiences without building infrastructure? What's the fastest way to launch travel experiences? Should I use the API or the White-Label Marketplace? Can travelers book directly on bridgify.io?
index-v2.html.all: Frequently asked questions What is Bridgify? Bridgify, part of HBX Group, is the infrastructure behind travel experiences. OTAs, airlines, hotels, banks, loyalty programs and super apps use it to offer 1M+ tours, attractions, activities and events in 180+ countries under their own brand, through one integration. What is experiences infrastructure? The layer between experience suppliers and the brands that sell to their customers. It connects many suppliers, normalizes their content into one schema and handles availability, booking and payments, so a brand sells tours, attractions, activities and events through one integration instead of one per supplier. Bridgify is the world's leading B2B travel experiences infrastructure. How do travel brands launch experiences without building infrastructure? They connect to an experiences infrastructure provider instead of each supplier. Bridgify aggregates and normalizes global supply and handles booking and payments. The brand either builds its own front end on the Experiences API or launches the White-Label Marketplace, which is ready-made. What's the fastest way to launch travel experiences? The White-Label Marketplace. It comes with search, experience pages, checkout, payments and 1M+ experiences already in place, needs no developers, and goes live in 3 days. You add your branding, domain and payment details. Should I use the API or the White-Label Marketplace? Use the Experiences API if your team wants to build the experience inside your own product. Use the White-Label Marketplace if you want a branded store without the build. Both run on the same supply, and many partners start with one and add the other. Can travelers book directly on bridgify.io? No. Bridgify works with businesses. Travelers book our partners' experiences inside the partners' own apps, sites and rewards programs.

api.html.text: Frequently asked questions How does the Bridgify Experiences API work? What is an API for travel? What is the difference between a travel API and a booking API? How do I choose the best API for activity inventory? Which experiences APIs offer real-time availability and pricing? Why not connect to a single marketplace directly? What is an attraction ticket API? What's the difference between an attraction ticket API and an activities API? How do I add attraction tickets to a travel app? What's the difference between a things-to-do API and a tours and activities API? Does the API include event tickets? How long does integration take?
api.html.all: Frequently asked questions How does the Bridgify Experiences API work? You integrate once. Bridgify connects to multiple global marketplaces, aggregators and suppliers, normalizes their content into one schema and returns search, availability, pricing and booking through a single API. Your team builds the interface; Bridgify manages the supply behind it. What is an API for travel? A travel API lets one system request travel content and bookings from another. A bank app, for example, can show live tours and take bookings without holding any supply itself. Bridgify's Experiences API covers tours, attractions, activities and events. What is the difference between a travel API and a booking API? "Travel API" is the broad term for any API that serves travel content, such as flights, hotels or experiences. A booking API is the part that confirms and manages reservations. The Experiences API does both for experiences: discovery content plus booking and cancellation. How do I choose the best API for activity inventory? Start with coverage: how many sources, destinations and categories are behind it. Then check real-time availability, content quality, and booking and cancellation handling. A multi-source API gives you more coverage and less dependence on one supplier. Which experiences APIs offer real-time availability and pricing? Look for one that checks availability and price live when the traveler searches and again at booking, not from a cached feed. Bridgify’s Experiences API returns real-time availability and pricing across 1M+ tours, attractions, activities and events from multiple suppliers, through one integration. Why not connect to a single marketplace directly? Going direct gives you one catalog on one supplier’s terms. The major marketplaces are strong networks, and they’re inside the Bridgify catalog. Bridgify gives you several of them, plus direct suppliers, through one integration and one schema. If you want the deepest relationship with one supplier, go direct. If you want coverage and flexibility, that’s what we do. What is an attraction ticket API? An API that lets a platform sell entry tickets to museums, landmarks, theme parks and other venues: availability, prices, booking and the ticket itself. The Experiences API covers attraction tickets alongside tours, activities and events, from multiple suppliers. What's the difference between an attraction ticket API and an activities API? An attraction ticket API sells entry to venues such as museums, landmarks and theme parks. An activities API sells things people do, such as tours, classes and day trips. Most travel brands need both. The Experiences API covers both, plus events, in one schema. How do I add attraction tickets to a travel app? Connect to an API that already holds attraction ticket supply, then build search, ticket pages and checkout in your app. With the Experiences API, that’s one integration for museums, landmarks and theme parks alongside tours and events. No developers? Link a White-Label Marketplace from your app instead. What's the difference between a things-to-do API and a tours and activities API? The terms overlap. "Things to do" is the traveler-facing term and usually covers attractions, tours, activities and events. "Tours and activities" is the supplier-side term. The Experiences API covers the full range. Does the API include event tickets? Yes. Live events, including concerts, sports and shows, sit alongside tours, attractions and activities. How long does integration take? It depends on how much of the journey you build yourself. Your team integrates one API instead of one per supplier, and our team supports you through it. If you need to launch without development, the White-Label Marketplace goes live in 3 days.

personalization.html.all: Frequently asked questions How do AI experience recommendations work? AIyelet reads traveler intent, profile and context, such as destination and travel style when available. It matches them against more than one million experiences and returns personalized recommendations instead of a generic list. Isn't a catalog of a million experiences just noise? Not with AIyelet on top. Bridgify organizes the supply into one clean schema, and AIyelet shows each traveler the few experiences that fit their destination, dates and travel style. What is intent-based search? Travelers describe what they want in their own words. "I want to do something romantic in Paris" returns relevant, bookable experiences, without the traveler choosing categories and filters first. Is there an AI-powered itinerary planner API for travel platforms? AIyelet is Bridgify's AI personalization layer for experiences. Given a destination, dates and traveler context, it recommends and ranks the experiences that fit and can arrange them within a day or a plan, inside your own product. It doesn't plan the full trip. Travelers can book experiences inside AI assistants now. Why add them to our own product? Inside an assistant, the traveler meets the marketplace's brand, and the customer relationship belongs to the marketplace. AIyelet puts the matching inside your product, so you keep the whole trip: the customer, their booking data and the chance to sell them the next experience. Can I offer personalized travel experiences without building a recommendation engine? Yes. AIyelet sits on top of Bridgify's supply, so recommendations come through the same integration as the experiences. You don't need to build or train your own model. Does personalization work with both the API and the White-Label Marketplace? Yes. AIyelet can power recommendations in your own product through the Experiences API, or inside the White-Label Marketplace under your brand.

Your developers call the API to search experiences, show details and complete bookings in your own interface. If you'd rather not build a front end, the White-Label Marketplace gives you a branded store instead. What are the best practices for travel API integration performance and uptime? Cache static content such as descriptions and images, and request live availability and price when the traveler searches and books. Handle timeouts and retries cleanly, and monitor booking errors. Our docs show how to do each of these with the Experiences API. What are the steps to implement an experiences API for travel agencies? 1. Agree on scope: markets, categories and where experiences appear. 2. Get credentials and test access. 3. Build search and experience pages. 4. Build the booking and cancellation flow. 5. Test end to end. 6. Go live, with monitoring. Is there an experiences API with secure payment and cancellation handling? Yes. The booking flow covers payment, confirmation and cancellation, and returns each experience's cancellation policy before checkout. With the API, payment runs through your own checkout; the White-Label Marketplace has payments built in.

otas.html.all: Frequently asked questions How do OTAs get one-contract access to experiences? Through an experiences infrastructure provider such as Bridgify. One commercial agreement and one integration give access to more than one million tours, attractions, activities and events from multiple global suppliers, instead of a contract and an API per marketplace. How should I evaluate experiences API suppliers that offer multi-source aggregation? Compare four things: the number and quality of supply sources; how content is mapped and de-duplicated; real-time availability and pricing; and enterprise support and SLAs. How does an experiences API integrate with booking engines? It plugs into your existing booking engine as another product line. Your engine calls it for search, availability, pricing and booking, then shows experiences next to flights and hotels in the same checkout, or as an add-on after booking. What are the best B2B travel API providers for tours, activities and experiences? It depends on the coverage you need. Single-source APIs give you one marketplace's catalog. A multi-source API such as Bridgify's combines several marketplaces, aggregators and direct suppliers behind one integration, so you get more coverage and less dependence on one source. Can we keep our existing marketplace connections? Yes. Many of the marketplaces OTAs already work with are inside the Bridgify catalog. You can keep your direct connections, run both, or move them into one integration. How can a smaller travel platform compete without a large catalog of tours? Connect to a multi-source catalog instead of building one. With Bridgify, a smaller platform offers the same 1M+ experiences in 180+ countries as a large one, from day one.

airlines.html.all: Frequently asked questions Frequently asked questions What is a destination experiences API? An API that gives an airline or travel brand bookable tours, attractions, activities and events at the passenger's destination. Bridgify's combines multiple suppliers behind one integration, so airlines sell experiences in their own channels without contracting local providers. What are the alternatives to a single-supplier destination experiences API? Airlines can contract one marketplace's API, build supplier connections in-house, or connect to a multi-source provider. Bridgify is the third option: multiple marketplaces, aggregators and suppliers in one normalized API, for wider destination coverage through one integration. How can airlines make ancillary revenue from tours and activities? Offer destination experiences where passengers already are: the booking flow, confirmation emails, manage-my-booking and the app. With Bridgify, airlines sell 1M+ experiences under their own brand without contracting suppliers or building the infrastructure. Where in the passenger journey should airlines offer experiences? At booking, while the trip is being planned. Before departure, when passengers research the destination. And on arrival, in the app. Can loyalty members redeem miles for experiences? Yes. Airlines can offer experiences as a miles redemption option, using the same infrastructure Bridgify runs for card and loyalty programs. Do we need to change our booking engine? No. Embed experiences through the API in your existing channels, or launch a branded experiences store that links from them.
